App Development Starter Kit

# You’re in. Here’s the fastest path to your first working integration.

Pick your entry point. Four paths, no prerequisites, no required order.

Your first API call

## Make your first API call in four simple steps

Pick the environment and follow the steps to make your first call to any DataForSEO API.

**The API Playground requires sign-in and spends real balance.** Every request you send from it is a real, billed call. The [Sandbox](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/sandbox/) is the only free route to practise on, and it answers with dummy data, not live results.

1. ### Get your credentials

   Sign in, open **API access**, and copy your API login and the generated API password — it is not the password you sign in with.

   `app.dataforseo.com/api-access`[How authentication works →](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/auth/)
2. ### What you are asking for

   Pick an API and an endpoint from the list on the left; the reference page for it explains every field the form shows you.

   [Endpoint reference for every API →](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/)
3. ### Send it

   **Live** endpoints answer inside the same response; **Standard** endpoints cost less, queue the work and hand you a task id.

   > Live for a handful of rows and anything a user is waiting on. Standard for volume — collect it with `tasks_ready`, or give the API a postback or pingback URL and stop polling.

   [Live vs Standard, and which to use →](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/live-vs-standard-method)
4. ### Read the response

   The response pane puts `status_code` and `status_message` above the data. `20000` means the result is ready; every other code tells you what the API did with the task.

   [Every status code and what it means →](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/errors/)

Developer toolbox

## Tools that will talk to DataForSEO APIs for you

Three ways in — client libraries, test environments, and AI agent integrations.

### Client libraries & examples

Use this when you want the HTTP plumbing handled for you.

- **Python**

  Generated client, installed with pip; each endpoint is a method call.

  [Repo ](https://github.com/dataforseo/PythonClient) [Docs examples ](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?python)
- **TypeScript**

  Same generated surface for Node, published to npm and typed throughout.

  [Repo ](https://github.com/dataforseo/TypeScriptClient) [Docs examples ](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?nodejs)
- **C# / .NET**

  NuGet package for .NET services, generated from the same specification.

  [Repo ](https://github.com/dataforseo/CSharpClient) [Docs examples ](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?csharp)
- **Java**

  Official Java client, generated from the same API specification.

  [Repo ](https://github.com/dataforseo/JavaClient)
- **PHP**

  Extensive PHP client library for DataForSEO APIs, maintained by our PHP developers.

  [PHP examples ](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?php)

Our documentation includes API call examples in cURL, PHP, Node JS, C#, and Python.

### Test & explore

Use this when you want to see a real response before you start building.

- Spends balance

  #### API Playground

  Build an API request in our graphic interface and get real data.

  [Dashboard →](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-playground/serp)
- Free

  #### Sandbox

  The same API with dummy data — practise without spending.

  [Docs →](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/sandbox/)
- #### Postman workspace

  Fork the official collection and run it with your credentials.

  [Postman →](https://www.postman.com/docs-dataforseo/dataforseo-api-v3/overview)
- #### OpenAPI specification

  One YAML for every endpoint — generate a client of your own.

  [GitHub →](https://github.com/dataforseo/OpenApiDocumentation/blob/master/openapi_specification.yaml)
- #### llms.txt

  The whole documentation tree in one file, useful for your AI agent.

  [Docs →](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/llms.txt)
- #### API reference

  Every endpoint and field, with a runnable example per language.

  [Docs →](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/)

## Implementation recommendations

Four decisions that shape every integration. Each line links to the material that goes deeper.

### Requests & queues

- **Choose Live or Standard first.** It decides your queue, your latency and your bill. [Live vs Standard](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/live-vs-standard-method)
- **Put up to 100 tasks in one Standard POST** instead of looping request by request. [Batching tasks](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/multiple-tasks-in-one-api-request)
- **Let a postback push results to your server.** Polling burns requests and adds delay. [Postbacks](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/pingbacks-postbacks-with-dataforseo-api)
- **Size your worker pool against the published limits** — several endpoints sit far below the general one. [Rate limits](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/rate-limits-and-request-limits)
- **Cap concurrency and set a real timeout on Live calls** — they hold the connection open. [Live endpoints](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/best-practices-live-endpoints-in-dataforseo-api)
- **Collect with Tasks Ready, not by re-requesting task IDs** — unless webhooks do it for you. [Tasks Ready](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/completed-tasks)

### Storage & refresh

- **Standard results stay retrievable for 30 days.** Live results are never stored. Persist them. [Result retention](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/how-long-do-you-keep-results)
- **Keep the raw response and derive metrics later** — recomputing is free, refetching is not. [A build, costed](https://dataforseo.com/blog/building-a-functioning-seo-tool-from-scratch-architecture-costs-lessons-learned)
- **Set a refresh cadence per endpoint.** Nothing else moves as fast as a ranking does. [Update frequency](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/how-often-is-dataforseo-api-data-updated)
- **Database-backed endpoints refresh on their own schedule,** separate from live search data. [Database refreshes](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/how-often-are-dataforseo-databases-updated)
- **Persist location and language codes, never display names** — each API has its own list. [Locations](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/dataforseo_labs/locations_and_languages/)
- **Reconcile your tables against the task list** before you trust a backfill. [Task reconciliation](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/export-dataforseo-tasks-with-id-list-endpoint)

### Reliability & errors

- **Map every status code into your logs before launch,** not during your first incident. [Status codes](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/errors/)
- **40101 is a search engine error — your request reached the engine, so there is no header to fix.** We already retried it several times; resubmit later rather than in a loop. [Error 40101](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/what-does-the-40101-error-mean)
- **Decide per code whether a retry can succeed.** A 40102 is a real answer — the engine has no results for those parameters — so change the request instead of resending it. [Error 40102](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/what-does-the-40102-error-mean)
- **Resend a lost webhook instead of paying for the task twice.** The resend is free. [Webhook resend](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/errors-and-webhook-resend-endpoints)
- **Poll the status endpoint before you page anyone** about an outage. [API Status](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/status/)
- **Whitelist your servers** so a leaked API password cannot be used elsewhere. [IP whitelisting](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/whitelist-ips)

### Cost control

- **Set a hard daily spend cap** in the dashboard — for all APIs, or one endpoint. [API Settings](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-settings)
- **Past the cap, tasks return 40203 until the UTC day rolls over.** Plan for it. [How the cap behaves](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/limit-my-payments)
- **Cap identical payloads per hour** so a retry loop cannot quietly drain the balance. [Duplicate limit](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/limit-duplicate-tasks)
- **Tag every task with a client, feature or job** so spend is attributable. [Usage tags](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/how-to-track-api-usage-with-tag)
- **Depth, mode and priority move the price more than volume does.** [What costs what](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/serp-api-cost-explained)
- **Read your failed task IDs on the dashboard’s errors screen** — codes and messages included. [Errors screen](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-errors)

## Frequently asked questions

### Where do I find my API login and password?

In the dashboard, under [API access](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access). The API password is generated automatically by DataForSEO and is different from your account password. [Authentication](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/auth/) is HTTP Basic and nothing else: there is no separate auth call, and credentials cannot be passed as URL parameters.

### Should I use Live or Standard endpoints?

[Live](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/live-vs-standard-method) returns the data in the same request, but holds the connection open until it is ready. Standard queues the task, costs less and scales better for bulk work. Pick one before you design the queue — it is the decision everything else hangs off.

### How do I collect Standard results without polling?

Set [postback_url](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/pingbacks-postbacks-with-dataforseo-api) when you create the task and we send the results to your server; set pingback_url and we notify you instead. If you use neither, the free [Tasks Ready](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/completed-tasks) endpoint lists completed tasks you have not collected yet.

### What are the rate limits, and how do I stay under them?

The general limit is [10,000 requests per minute](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/rate-limits-and-request-limits), and several endpoints are far lower — Live Google Ads allows 12 per minute. Before you add concurrency, put up to [100 tasks in a single Standard POST](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/multiple-tasks-in-one-api-request); that is the cheapest throughput you will find.

### Can I test the API without spending money?

Yes. Send the same request to [sandbox.dataforseo.com](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/sandbox/) and it is free, though the response is generic sample data rather than real results. The [API Playground](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/dataforseo-api-explorer) in the dashboard is the opposite: it makes real calls and charges you for each one.

### How long are my results available?

[Standard task results are kept for 30 days](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/how-long-do-you-keep-results) and can be collected repeatedly in that window; SERP HTML results are kept for 7 days. Live results are not stored at all, so write them to your own database as they arrive.

## Credentials in hand. Go make the call.

Send one real request from the Playground to see the response shape, then look the fields up in the reference.

Playground calls are billable · the Sandbox is free · talk to support
